dataLabel: the least an Observation can be
comment: Everything in <ObservationShape> is optional but :subject, so this is the whole of a conforming Observation.  Each example below adds one thing to it.
The query map is core ShapeMap: every node with a :status, and a claim that the patient is *not* an Observation.
Every element the schema knows, in one document.

dataLabel: the same measurement, in two documents
comment: A graph is not a file: the observation comes from an instrument, the patient from a registry, and they meet at the IRI one names and the other describes.  The tabs are named after what each document says it is, and hovering a constraint whose match is in the other document brings that document forward to highlight it.
The one thing an Observation must have.

dataLabel: a status outside the value set
a birthdate that is a dateTime
comment: A date and a dateTime are different datatypes, however alike they read.

dataLabel: a quantity with no number and no code
comment: Quantity :value is required and :system is contingent on :code

dataLabel: a gender outside the value set
two documents, and the mistake is in the second
data:
PREFIX : <http://hl7.org/fhir/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
BASE <http://hl7.example/>

# Observation
<Obs1>
  :status  "final" ;
  :subject <Patient2> .
PREFIX : <http://hl7.org/fhir/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
BASE <http://hl7.example/>

# Patient
<Patient2>
  :name   "Bob" ;
  :gender "M" .
comment: Validating the observation walks into the patient, so a bad gender code in the second document fails the first.  Hovering the failure switches to the document that caused it.
Douglas Adams, validated by asking query.wikidata.org for each neighborhood as the walk needs it.

dataLabel: Q42, Q76 from the JSON API
comment: The same entity, and Q76 with it, from the JSON pages Wikidata is edited through, turned back into the RDF the query service would serve.  The QueryMap names entities by id and lets this source work out what they are called.

The same entity from a page downloaded earlier: edit it in the pane to see what an edit would validate as before making it.  With a downloaded site table too (the sitelinks in a page name wikis like "enwiki", and only that table says which URL and language that is), this entry needs no network at all.

dataLabel: BRCA1, its chromosome and its assembly
comment: GeneWiki's human gene schema (EntitySchema:E37), with the two schemas it imports inlined: a gene's chromosome is E109's and the genome assembly its coordinates are given against is E108's.  So validating BRCA1 (Q227339) walks from the gene to chromosome 17 (Q220677) and on to GRCh38 (Q20966585) -- three entities, three shapes, each page fetched as the walk reaches it.  Four constraints are relaxed here, each marked RELAXED IN THIS COPY where it stands: three are places where the data cites a source the schema enumerates without (a newer Ensembl release, the OMA browser), and one is a normalized value this source can't derive from an entity page.

A dataset with a housekeeping graph: `GRAPH <CardCatalog>` scopes the ^ex:manages arc and the whole catalog entry into it, the way a SPARQL `GRAPH <CardCatalog> { ... }` block would (doc/datasets.md).
The same entry written into the default graph: the constraint speaks only of <CardCatalog>, so the arc is missing where the schema looks.

`GRAPH TERM` follows each matched value into the graph of the same name: the chromosome record in GRAPH gene:BRCA1-chr17, each UniProt reference in the graph named for it.  The gene's own arcs stay in the default graph.

data:
PREFIX gene: <http://example.org/gene/>
PREFIX prov: <http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#>
PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX uniprot: <http://uniprot.org/uniprot/>
PREFIX uniprotRef: <http://uniprot.org/ref/>

gene:BRCA1
  gene:product gene:BRCA1-encodes-001 .

gene:BRCA1-encodes-001
  gene:encodes uniprot:P38398 ;
  prov:wasDerivedFrom uniprotRef:P38398 .

# the reference record strayed into the default graph
uniprotRef:P38398 ex:id "P38398" ;
  ex:when "2024-01-15T09:30:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime .
comment: The reference's record must live in the graph named after it; written into the default graph it is outside the view `GRAPH TERM` switches to, so ex:id and ex:when are missing there.

Each profile document is a graph; `GRAPH FRAGMENT` follows <https://bob.example/card#me> into <https://bob.example/card>.  Alice and Bob know each other, and the cycle terminates the way recursive shapes always have.
Bob claims to know Carol, but no graph <https://carol.example/card> describes her: the foaf:knows arc matches the constraint's predicate and its value fails in the graph the schema says to look in.
